prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, home type, budget, preferred brands and timeline. If you share your Atlanta ZIP code and a few details (age/size of your home, whether you want a particular brand, and your budget) I can give a tailored short list and recent review summary.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical way to find the best replacement contractor and a few reputable names that serve Atlanta.

Reputable companies that serve Atlanta (good starting point)
- Coolray (Atlanta-based, large local presence)
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin (franchises)
- ARS/Rescue Rooter
- Aire Serv (local franchises)

(These are established companies with broad coverage — many independent local contractors can be equal or better depending on your neighborhood. I can find top-rated independents near you if you give a ZIP.)

How to choose the best contractor (checklist)
1. Licensing & insurance — Verify they carry liability insurance and workers’ comp and are legally allowed to work in Georgia.
2. Certifications — Look for NATE-certified technicians and EPA 608 certification for refrigerant handling.
3. Load calculation — They should perform a Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old size”) to size the new system properly.
4. Written estimate — Get 2–3 detailed, itemized written quotes showing equipment model, SEER rating, labor, permit fees, duct work, and removal of old unit.
5. Permits & code compliance — Contractor should pull required permits and handle inspections.
6. Manufacturer credentials & warranty — Ask if they’re a factory-authorized dealer for your preferred brand and confirm both unit and labor warranties in writing.
7. References & reviews — Check Google, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB for recent reviews; ask the company for local references.
8. Duct and airflow assessment — Good contractors will inspect ducts, perform airflow tests, and recommend fixes if needed.
9. Financing & rebates — Ask about financing, utility rebates, and available incentives for high-efficiency systems.
10. Timeline & cleanup — Get a start/completion date and confirm they’ll remove and dispose of the old equipment.

Typical cost range (Atlanta, 2024–2025 ballpark)
- Small home (2–3 ton) basic replacement: $4,000–$7,000
- Larger or higher-efficiency (14–18+ SEER) systems: $6,000–$12,000+
- Complex replacements (ductwork, custom installs): $10,000–$20,000+
Actual cost varies by home size, ductwork condition, brand, and SEER.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?
- What exact equipment model are you proposing and its SEER?
- What’s included in the price (permit, labor, thermostat, refrigerant, disposal)?
- What are the unit and labor warranty terms?
- Are you licensed, insured, and NATE-certified?
- Can you provide recent local references or reviews?
- How long will the job take and when can you start?

Next step
If you give your ZIP code and a little info about your home (square footage or number of bedrooms, whether ducts are metal/old, and any brand preference), I’ll compile a 3–5 contractor shortlist in your area with their strengths, average estimate ranges, and links to reviews so you can contact the best fit.
